subject: Agriculture
title: IR8 and the Rice Miracle
description: A quick, practical guide to IR8 and the Rice Miracle.

hook.text: In 1966, IRRI in the Philippines released IR8—a rice variety that yielded twice as much as traditional types.

buildup.text: IR8 was semi-dwarf, like Borlaug's wheat. Short stalks held heavy grain without falling over.

discovery.text: With fertilizer, IR8 could produce 10 tons per hectare—unheard of for rice at the time.

twist.text: IR8 didn't taste great. Farmers grew it for yield but ate traditional varieties when they could afford to.

climax.text: Later varieties like IR36 and IR64 combined high yield with better taste and disease resistance.

punchline.text: IR8 fed millions. Its successors fed billions.

quiz.question: What was special about the IR8 rice variety?
options: It was semi-dwarf and yielded twice as much as traditional rice
